summary: Trump announced cancellation of a planned attack on Iran after a preliminary agreement framework including immediate full opening of the Strait of Hormuz and an end to Iran's nuclear threat, with Israel joining the commitment. Iran's nuclear negotiating team denied any agreement on reopening the Strait, stating it remains closed while hostile US actions continue. Israel raised its alert to the highest level amid reports of a possible US strike on Iranian energy facilities.
key_points: Trump stated he agreed to cancel an attack on Iran at the request of Iran and regional countries to allow a framework agreement that includes immediate full opening of the Strait of Hormuz and an end to Iran's nuclear threat, with Israel joining the commitment. (Source: @VahidOnline/77702)

A source close to Iran's nuclear negotiating team told Fars there is no agreement on reopening the Strait of Hormuz; the Strait remains closed as long as hostile US actions continue, and ship movement is only possible via the announced route with IRGC naval permission. (Source: @rasedal3ado138e/382533)

Israel has been placed on the highest state of alert with senior political and security officials holding consultations throughout the weekend, according to Channel 12. (Source: @Faytuks_Network/6002)

The IDF raised alert for possible escalation in Iran; the US advised citizens to leave the Middle East amid reports Trump is considering a powerful attack on Iranian energy facilities. (Source: @amitsegal/63542)
IDF Brigade 401 completed its 8-month mission in South Lebanon, confiscating over 600 weapons and eliminating more than 60 Hezbollah terrorists. (Source: @idf_telegram/24808)

Iranian advisor Mohammad Marandi warned that based on Trump administration statements, tonight may be the last night of normality for Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Bahrain, UAE, and possibly Oman, threatening destruction of their key infrastructures if Iranian civilian infrastructure is attacked. (Source: @New_security8200/203141)

Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman pressured Trump in a phone call to de-escalate and stop a planned attack on Iran; Qatari mediators are separately engaging Iranian, US, and Omani officials on reopening the Strait of Hormuz. (Source: @VahidOnline/77701, @asafroz/52192)

Attacks were reported on Kurdish party headquarters in Sulaymaniyah, Iraqi Kurdistan; interception attempts occurred in Erbil; explosions were heard in Sulaymaniyah. (Source: @kianmeli1/90513, @lelotsenzura/94025, @shin_persian/8781)

sections.threat_assessment: The simultaneous announcement by Trump of a halted attack and a framework agreement, contradicted by Iran's denial of any Strait of Hormuz deal, creates a dangerous ambiguity. Iran's explicit threat to target Gulf state infrastructures if its civilian facilities are struck, combined with Israel's highest alert posture and US citizen evacuation advisory, indicates a high probability of miscalculation. The reported IRGC military reconstitution during the ceasefire and distribution of ammunition to government buildings suggest preparation for asymmetric warfare. Meanwhile, ongoing kinetic actions in Lebanon, Iraq, and Gaza demonstrate multiple active fronts that could be triggered by any escalation.
sections.regional_response: Saudi Arabia, Qatar, and Oman are actively mediating to prevent a regional conflagration, with Riyadh directly pressuring Washington and Doha engaging Tehran and Washington separately on the Strait of Hormuz. The Gulf states face explicit Iranian threats of infrastructure destruction, compelling them to seek de-escalation while balancing US alliance commitments. Jordan is implicitly included in Iranian threat calculus. The US maintains maximum military readiness while pursuing diplomatic off-ramps, but mixed signals from Trump and Iranian officials undermine confidence in a stable framework.
sections.intelligence_notes: Key intelligence gaps include the veracity of the claimed framework agreement, the operational status of IRGC preparations for guerrilla warfare, and the extent of Hamas rearmament in Gaza. The tracking of US strategic airlift over Palestine suggests logistical preparation for potential contingency operations. Monitoring of Kurdish party attacks in Sulaymaniyah and interception attempts in Erbil may indicate Iranian proxy activity or internal Iraqi dynamics. The IDF's completion of its South Lebanon mission may signal a force posture shift toward the Iranian threat axis.
